review_notes:
I read the whole 64-line file. It has two theorems.

1. `mem_centralizer_range_weightTorusPoints_iff_isDiag` is tagged `@[simp]`. The left side is `g ∈ Subgroup.centralizer (Set.range (weightTorusPoints k))` and the right side is `IsDiag` of the coerced matrix. The rewrite goes from the more complex membership to the more primitive predicate, so it should terminate. The only competing rule I looked for was `mem_centralizer_iff`. In Mathlib's `Algebra/Group/Center.lean` it is a plain `lemma`, not `@[simp]`, so it does not compete.
2. `centralizer_range_weightTorusPoints_eq_comap_diagonalTorus` is not `@[simp]`, which looks right. Making it simp would compete with the first lemma on `centralizer` expressions. Its proof uses `simp only` with the first lemma, `Subgroup.mem_comap`, `Subgroup.subtype_apply` and `mem_diagonalTorus_iff`. The last of these is `@[simp]` in `LinearAlgebra/Matrix/GeneralLinearGroup/Diagonal/Basic.lean` and rewrites diagonal-torus membership to `IsDiag`, so both sides reduce to the same normal form.

The same pattern appears in the E6, E7, doubled-E6, type-B and type-D siblings, including `@[simp]` on the membership lemma. I found no evidence of a cycle, a competing rule or a missing canonical lemma. I did not run Lean, so this is based on reading the sources only. I found no finding that meets the rubric.
